Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with ~1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain, and possible hematuria; impression of uncomplicated cystitis; plan for urine testing and short-course antibiotics.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging on urination with increased frequency and suprapubic ache (worse with voiding) for just under a week; pink-tinged urine noted today.
- Associated symptoms/ROS: No back/flank pain. No nausea/vomiting. No fevers. No abnormal vaginal discharge. Baseline IBS bowel pattern unchanged.
- Pertinent negatives: No new bowel symptoms. Denies systemic symptoms.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented). IBS medication (name unclear; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Clindamycin – reaction not specified.
- Social history: University student living in halls with a flatmate. Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; does not use condoms; last unprotected intercourse ~1–2 weeks ago. Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago. Drinks alcohol socially. Tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago; does not smoke tobacco.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Impression:
- Likely acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) with possible hematuria. No features suggestive of pyelonephritis based on history.

Plan:
- Antibiotics: 3-day course discussed (trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin); specific agent and dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Urine testing: Provide urine sample at practice for dip and laboratory analysis; clinic to contact with results and tailor antibiotics if needed.
- Supportive care: Increase oral fluids.
- Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.
- Safety net: Seek care if fever, back pain, or vomiting develop. Return if symptoms not improving by next week.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals or physical exam documented. No pregnancy test documented. No STI screening documented. Specific antibiotic choice and dosing not documented. IBS medication name and dosing not documented. Allergy reaction details not described.
- Internal conflicts: Symptom duration initially stated as 3 days, then corrected to “just under a week” (conflict noted). Sexual activity initially denied, then confirmed (conflict noted). Hematuria described as pink urine; uncertainty about frank blood.
- Transcript quality: Some unclear/inaudible portions; medication name not captured; otherwise adequate.
